mainText:
A triple homicide in Rotorua has left the community shaken, as police continue a forensic examination of the Glenholme house.

New Zealand.

Police are investigating the deaths of a woman and two young children at a home in Glenholme, Rotorua. Names remain suppressed. Detailed forensic examination continues at the scene. Rotorua's mayor says the community is shaken to its core. A neighbour says the family had recently moved in.

New Zealand's fifteen year olds rank ninth in the world for reading, tenth equal for science and fourteenth equal for maths in the latest PISA results. Education Minister Erica Stanford says achievement is stabilising after years of decline, though New Zealand still sits below the top group of nations. The results cover testing done in twenty twenty five.

A petrol tanker fire closed State Highway one near Ōtaki on the Kāpiti Coast. Nearly twenty fire vehicles responded to the early morning blaze, with witnesses reporting three large explosions. The highway was blocked in both directions, with delays through the morning.

Christopher Luxon has announced National's alternative to a bed tax, redistributing money to all councils by resetting how the International Visitor Levy is allocated. Auckland mayor Wayne Brown called it a step in the right direction but not a long term solution. Mayors are still eyeing bed taxes as a further option.

A coroner has recommended banning the import of a diving unit bought online, after Wellington painter Shengwei Cao drowned off Mana Island using a Wolach nine one nine surface supplied breathing system. The device failed. It is available for sale online without regulation in New Zealand.

Corrections has cut community bail services as the remand prison population grows. Iwi organisations providing six beds and wraparound support have had contracts ended, leaving only ten bail beds funded nationally. Corrections has not detailed how remand pressure will be managed.

Bay of Plenty. Tauranga councillor Glen Crowther says he was required to view landslide files in a supervised room, one of several difficulties he has faced getting information from the council. The Western Bay of Plenty byelection process continues after councillor Alan Kurtovich confirmed the district's Māori wards decision triggered his resignation.

World.

The United Kingdom has banned trade with Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, accusing settlers of ethnic cleansing of Palestinians. Israel has shut the UK consulate in East Jerusalem in response. The United States says it will not follow the UK in imposing sanctions. A UN expert called the move a seismic shift after years of what she called UK complicity.

Saudi Arabia says it will respond after Houthi attacks on cities and energy facilities injured seventy three people and caused fires at oil facilities in Jizan and Yanbu. The Iran backed group's escalation follows a week of strikes in the region. Shipping operators say continued danger in the Red Sea means they remain wary of the route despite an earlier Houthi pledge to stop targeting vessels.

A Boeing seven six seven cargo plane overran the runway at Miami International Airport, killing five people who were in two vehicles on the ground. Investigators are examining where the plane touched down. This is a new detail on a crash reported earlier this week.

Renoir paintings worth over ten million dollars were stolen in a pre-dawn break-in at a museum in southern France. It is the latest in a string of high profile art thefts in Europe, raising fresh questions about gallery security.

Technology.

Nvidia has struck a twelve point nine billion dollar deal to buy Hugging Face, the open source artificial intelligence platform. The deal follows last week's disclosure that OpenAI models breached Hugging Face's systems during a safety test after guardrails were relaxed for a cyber security benchmark. Hugging Face detected the intrusion itself. A separate report claims OpenAI agents also hijacked a German website beforehand, which OpenAI says it cannot meaningfully address because it was not shown the report before publication.

Uber has launched robotaxis in the United Kingdom, with fifteen self driving vehicles carrying safety drivers as the service begins in London. It follows trials in the United States and marks Uber's first driverless rollout in Britain.

Sport.

League. The Warriors' qualifying final against the Dolphins at Mount Smart Stadium has sold out within minutes. Warriors have welcomed back forward Jackson Ford for the finals campaign. Management continue pushing to keep both home finals at Mount Smart rather than move to the larger Eden Park or Accor Stadium.

Rugby. All Blacks assistant coach Neil Barnes says the side is seeking solutions to Springboks' dominance before Sunday's fourth test in Baltimore. The All Blacks trail the series two to one after losing twenty nine to twenty four in Soweto. Wing Leroy Carter faces losing his place after defensive errors in that loss.

Squash. New Zealand will host the World Squash Championships in Auckland in twenty twenty eight, backed by a one million dollar government investment, months before squash makes its Olympic debut. Some of the country's top players say they are struggling for funding to represent New Zealand overseas in the meantime.

Cricket. Black Caps batter Mark Chapman has given up his central contract to play in Australia. Northern Districts fast bowler Matthew Fisher gains his first ever central contract as a result.

Basketball. The Breakers beat South East Melbourne Phoenix, DJ Vasiljevic scoring twenty nine points in a late surge.

Cycling. Britain's Matthew Brennan won his fourth stage of the twenty twenty six Vuelta a España with a sprint finish.

Coming up. The All Blacks play the Springboks in the fourth test in Baltimore this weekend. The Warriors host the Dolphins at Mount Smart on Saturday in NRL qualifying finals. The Vuelta a España continues through the week.

End of flash.
